summary: Chaikin Oscillator: the 3-bar EMA minus the 10-bar EMA of the Accumulation/Distribution line, around zero.
overview: The Chaikin Oscillator shows the momentum of the Accumulation/Distribution line, in its own pane around zero.
The line and fill are green above zero (accumulation) and red below (distribution).
how: Chaikin Oscillator = EMA(A/D, 3) - EMA(A/D, 10). The A/D line is the running total of volume weighted by where each bar closes in its range.
Both EMA lengths can be changed. Because it uses the A/D line, it reacts to where each bar closes in its range, not only to the close-to-close change.
use: Some traders watch zero-line crosses as changes in buying or selling pressure.
Look for divergence between the oscillator and price.
Use it with a trend filter to read crosses in context.
Compare it with MACD to see momentum from volume rather than price.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
It can move against price when closes sit low in rising bars.
